subject: URGENT: HelioMaps - inference latency & error burst (possible VPC/DNS path issue)
messages:
From: Suhail Khan <suhail@heliomaps.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Nov 2025 08:14:02 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden latency + 5xx spike on inference (started ~07:50 UTC)

Marissa / Ben —

We just hit a serious regression in production starting ~07:50 UTC. Our inference requests to Redwood are seeing: 
- P95 -> P99 jump from ~1.2s to ~7.8s
- 5xx rate climbed to ~15% for the last 20 minutes
- Throughput has collapsed on a handful of endpoints (peak qps down ~60%)

Attached is a short snapshot of traces and a sample error log (error_snaps_1122.png, helio_incident_log_1122.zip). We pushed no config changes on our side; the only thing that changed in our infra was a CloudProxy maintenance window that reported a config reload at 07:46 UTC.

This is impacting checkout flows for ~12% of our users — they’re blocking the release. Can Redwood confirm whether this is on your side and whether there’s any known routing/peering issue?

Suhail
Site Reliability — HelioMaps
ops@heliomaps.com

Suhail — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. We’ve opened an urgent internal investigation. Initial asks while we triage: 
- Can you confirm whether your CloudProxy is doing any DNS rewrites or additional outbound NAT for calls to api.redwood.com?
- If you can, please capture a short tcpdump for requests to api.redwood.com from one of the affected hosts and drop it in the shared Drive link (I’ll send one moment).

I’m looping in Jonas (SRE lead) and Ben (AE) so we can coordinate with your team and cloud provider. Our immediate plan: 1) triage whether this is a path/asymmetry/DNS issue, 2) open a provider ticket if so, 3) if we confirm the path traverses a proxy/NAT causing replays/timeouts we’ll propose a temporary routing fallback (dedicated pool or region pin) to get you back to acceptable SLOs while the provider remediates.

I’ll send an update within 30 minutes.

—Marissa

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: se an_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Nov 2025 09:05:41 -0800
Subject: RE: Production: sudden latency + 5xx spike on inference (started ~07:50 UTC)

Marissa / Ben — quick tech findings from the first 20 minutes of captures and our edge telemetry: 

Summary: evidence points at an asymmetric path where a subset of HelioMaps’ requests are being routed through a CloudProxy hop that performs NAT + TLS termination for outbound connections. That hop is introducing additional TLS handshakes / connection churn and inconsistent DNS answers across AZs which is forcing retries and long queuing in our front-side proxies. We saw: 
- Multiple TCP retransmit bursts and SYN retries for the same client IPs (pcap_sample_1122.txt attached)
- DNS A record for api.redwood.com returned two different IP sets from HelioMaps’ resolver cluster during the window (likely stale cache / split-horizon)
- Requests that followed the normal peering path show baseline latency; the ones routed via CloudProxy show large tail and 5xx rates

Immediate actions recommended: 
1) HelioMaps: request CloudProxy temporarily bypass/red-blacklist api.redwood.com so requests take the normal peering path (fastest mitigation).
2) Redwood: provision a dedicated-capacity canary and shift ~20% of HelioMaps traffic to that pool (we can do this via route override for the account) — this gives immediate stability while provider fixes the path.
3) Joint: open an escalation with CloudProxy + interconnect provider immediately (we’ll prepare packet captures & timing).

We can implement (2) in ~30–45 minutes if approved; (1) depends on HelioMaps’ change window. I’ll keep digging on root cause but the DNS split + proxy NAT looks like the primary driver.

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Exec update: HelioMaps production impact — recommended mitigation and ask for approval

Team / Sean —

Quick executive summary and ask (for leadership visibility): HelioMaps hit a production incident this morning with high tail latency and elevated 5xxs. Investigation shows the traffic from their affected hosts is intermittently being routed through CloudProxy, which performs NAT/TLS termination and is yielding inconsistent DNS answers and connection churn. This appears to be a provider-side path / proxy interoperability issue; not an application bug in Redwood.

What we did: 
- Confirmed asymmetry & DNS split via pcap/edge telemetry.
- Prepared a dedicated-capacity canary and route override that will shift ~20% of HelioMaps traffic off the flaky path. Implementation ETA: ~45 minutes pending approval.
- Prepared packet capture + timing artifacts for HelioMaps and CloudProxy to expedite provider escalation (link: https://drive.redwood/HelioMaps/incident-1122).

Ask: 
1) Approve emergency capacity shift to dedicated pool for HelioMaps for the next 48 hours (this will likely increase their bill, but I propose offering a one-time service credit for the disruption).
2) Sign-off to escalate to CloudProxy via our channel and request they bypass api.redwood.com or roll back the config that triggered the reload at 07:46 UTC.

Customer impact: critical for ~12% of HelioMaps’ checkouts; failure to act will continue to hit revenue flows.

I recommend we approve the capacity shift and initiate the provider escalation now. If Sean is not available, Ben: can you confirm AE sign-off on the temporary credit and contract exception so we can move fast?

Thanks — I’ll wait for a quick ack and then kick off the change. Included below: original customer note and Jonas’ technical summary.
